headline: High-risk default interaction: n8n can write and execute workflows against broad-network Chatwoot data, creating leakage, conflict, and cascading-action risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Chatwoot exposes customer messages and integrations, while n8n can ingest workflow inputs and route them through nodes. A shared filesystem or copied message content could let attacker-controlled text from Chatwoot influence n8n workflows, though no direct shared channel is documented. The pathway is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF Chatwoot message content is copied into an n8n workflow input
IF n8n parses that content as instructions or node parameters
mitigations: Add a strict content-to-command separator in the workflow
Strip markdown and code blocks before passing text onward
Use allowlisted node parameters only
Review any workflow that ingests customer messages
requires-engineering: add provenance tags between systems

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, and orders, while n8n has broad network egress and can read/write the server filesystem. In default automation setups, n8n can move those data classes into third-party integrations or logs, creating a realistic exfiltration path from Chatwoot through n8n.
conditions: IF an n8n workflow receives Chatwoot customer records or messages
IF that workflow sends them to an external integration or stores them on disk
mitigations: Disable unnecessary outbound integrations
Mask customer identifiers before workflow handoff
Restrict filesystem access to a dedicated workspace
Audit logs for payload capture
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Chatwoot can emit support data while n8n can write files and execute shell commands on the server. If both operate on the same workspace or connected systems, they can overwrite artifacts or race on shared state. Chatwoot does not show write primitives, so this is overlap-driven rather than a full write-write conflict.
conditions: IF both agents target the same filesystem directory or connected system
IF n8n workflows mutate artifacts derived from Chatwoot outputs
mitigations: Separate workspaces per workflow
Lock shared files before writes
Use append-only logs for handoffs
Disable shell steps for shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: n8n is explicitly an orchestrator with AI Agent nodes and tool-use patterns, so it can treat upstream outputs as actionable inputs. Chatwoot can supply customer-facing text and reports that n8n may forward into integrations without verification, making erroneous or malicious content propagate into downstream actions.
conditions: IF n8n workflows use Chatwoot outputs as authoritative inputs
IF downstream nodes send emails, tickets, or API updates without validation
mitigations: Insert a human approval step before actions
Validate structured fields against a schema
Require source attribution on every handoff
Limit AI Agent nodes to read-only analysis
requires-engineering: add verification gates before side effects

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot clearly handles customer data and interaction history, while n8n processes whatever the workflow touches and stores credentials on its server. That creates a compliance mismatch risk if regulated customer data is routed into n8n workflows with different retention or residency controls; the profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction breach, so medium is the higher defensible level.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is routed from Chatwoot into n8n
IF n8n retention or hosting differs from Chatwoot policy
mitigations: Classify data before workflow entry
Shorten retention on workflow executions
Store secrets only in approved credential stores
Document residency for each integration
requires-engineering: align retention and DPA terms
